title: Mass on a spring

slow_motion.evidence: No narration, captions, or on-screen text indicate slow motion; motion appears as a continuous animation.

subjects.description: small solid red rectangular mass attached to the bottom end of the white zig-zag spring

observation.what_happens: A red block suspended from a spring oscillates vertically, moving between a lower stretched-spring position and an upper compressed-spring position. The oscillation is already in progress at the start of the clip and continues uninterrupted to the end with no visible release or stop.

calibration.note: no scale: lengths are in pixels

reasoning: The track is 1D vertical with s spanning 0-217 pix and x ~0, showing ~1.6 s period oscillations whose envelope shrinks from ~108 to ~70 pix, so a ~3.9 rad/s oscillator with weak damping. Candidates go from ideal SHM to linear viscous damping to linear plus quadratic air drag to cubic Duffing stiffness to test decay type and nonlinearity.

caveats: Positions are in pixels with no real scale, so rest point and wobble are video units.
Damping is modeled as smooth viscous friction, ignoring stick or airflow quirks.
Only steady mid-oscillation is shown, so behavior after stopping or large pulls is untested.
critique.finding: The block swings on its spring with natural wobble {omega} around rest spot {s_eq}. It slowly loses energy to friction set by {gamma}.
critique.headline: The spring block bounces, slowly losing height.
critique.why_it_won: Simple viscous slowing captures the shrinking swings while extra cubic stiffness adds only wobble.

headline: The spring block bounces, slowly losing height.
finding: The block swings on its spring with natural wobble 4 ± 1.44e-4 rad/s around rest spot 111 ± 0.014 pix. It slowly loses energy to friction set by 0.12 ± 2.89e-4 1/s.

eyeball.confidence: low - visual period/amplitude guessed from few frames without explicit timebase
eyeball.law_in_words: Vertical damped harmonic motion about gravity-stretched equilibrium: acceleration = -omega^2*(s - s_eq) - gamma*velocity
